articleTitle: Developing a Chatbot for College Student Programme Advisement
abstract: Elective course selection often challenges students to make decisions concerning their academic interests and other practical issues such as graduation plan, class scheduling, and difficulty of course content. Conversations with academic advisors and peers are usually considered as a useful process for obtaining official and informal information, rearranging priorities, and making compromise in the decision. The paper describes the design and development of a conversational agent called EASElective for elective course selection. EASElective is designed to complement existing academic advising services with an online natural language interactive interface that will support a conversation on topics from basic official course data to informal students' opinions. The major design components of EASElective include intent detection, routines for conversation management, dialogue design, sustainable students' opinion collection and analysis, and course information management. The paper also describes a study on the perceived usefulness of EASElective. The findings were found to be largely positive and EASElective has unique functions and characteristics when compared to other conventional academic advising services.

Author Keywords: academic advising, conversational agents, chatbots, cloud computing, elective course selection

articleTitle: Comparative Study on the Pedagogical Use of Interactive Spherical Video-Based Virtual Reality: The EduVenture-VR Experience
abstract: This work aimed to look into teachers' concerns about the feasibility of adopting Interactive Spherical Video-based Virtual Reality (ISVVR), with the use of EduVenture-VR as a case study. We collected categorical data from ninety secondary school teachers among three different teaching groups. The comparative analysis between groups was conducted. The results showed that "perceived students' learning motivation" and "perceived students' learning performance" would influence teachers' concerns about the feasibility of adopting ISVVR.

articleTitle: A Gamification Technique for Motivating Students to Learn Code Readability in Software Engineering
abstract: Code readability is one of the important software quality attributes that computer science students need to learn in their programming classes, unfortunately most of the students do not have the necessary work experience or background to appreciate the importance of code readability. Traditional methods of learning code readability tend to be less than interactive and practical in the classroom environment. With the advent of gamification technique, this study introduced a new interactive teaching method and implemented as GamiCRS, an online platform for students to learn code readability. The focus was on incorporating game-based mechanisms to enable students with positive attitudes towards a more interesting learning process. A complete incentive and reward model is proposed in the study together with a combination of both intrinsic and extrinsic motivators identified. To ensure its dynamic efficacy, a field experiment was carried out to compare GamiCRS with its non-gamified counterparts and to evaluate learning outcomes. The empirical results show a positive effect towards the application of GamiCRS in the classroom environment. As many learning activities in software engineering are typically challenging and seldom amusing, gamification can thus be applied as a compelling addition to supporting a wider variety of teaching tactics.

articleTitle: Learning Analytics Intervention: A Review of Case Studies
abstract: Intervention has been claimed to be the greatest challenge in learning analytics. As the provision of just-in-time and personalised support for learners, intervention has yet to be widely implemented in learning analytics practices. This paper reviews intervention practices in higher education in 23 case studies. The cases were categorised into four types – direct message, actionable feedback, categorisation of students, and course redesign – according to the nature of the methods of intervention; and the intervention methods were summarised. Most of the intervention cases belonged to the first two types. Direct message involves contacting at-risk students via channels such as emails or phone calls to encourage their participation, provide additional learning resources, or remind them of deadlines. Actionable feedback involves the provision of suggestions or information for students to help them understand their performance and possible ways of improving it. Only a few cases were identified for the other two types of intervention, which involve categorisation of students into different groups based on their risk levels for taking specific remedial actions for each group, and redesigning the course structure or contents based on the analysis of data. The results of this review serve to facilitate the formulation of intervention strategies for higher education institutions which practise learning analytics.

articleTitle: The Measurement and Determinants of Student Satisfaction of Education Informatization in Chinese Universities
abstract: Education informatization often refers to develop educational resources and to optimize the educational process by using information technology so as to enhance the academic performance of students. However, whether this kind of education meets the satisfaction of students also should not be overlooked. This paper first focuses on how to measure the satisfaction of education informatization for students in Chinese higher education institution. Furthermore, taking into account different types of university students' satisfaction with education informatization, this study attempts to analyze the mechanism behind the impact of student satisfaction and try to provide a scientific basis for colleges and universities to improve the blended learning. Meanwhile, the study analyzes the impact mechanisms of high satisfaction students and low satisfaction students. Using cross-sectional data from 3,312 students in China, structural equation modeling(SEM) and multivariable linear regression model are employed to developed and analyzed. The results indicate that: (I) nearly half of the students are satisfied with the education informatization in their institutions while the number of high satisfaction groups and that of low satisfaction groups are basically similar; (II) from the perspective of different school types, the number of high satisfaction groups in didactical universities are significantly higher than that in investigative universities; (III) ICT usages, teaching process and instructional design, in general, are key determinants of the satisfaction of university education informatization; (IV) the group of students with high satisfaction seem to be more easily influenced by the interactive feedback between teachers and students and the effect of teaching organization while the low degree of satisfaction were usually attributed to the usage quality, course quality and academic development. It is recommended in this study that universities should pay more attention to the improvement of ICT application strategies and the innovation of blended learning evaluation.

Author Keywords: Education Informatization, Student Satisfaction, Impact Mechanism, Low Satisfaction, High Satisfaction

articleTitle: The Use of 360-Degree Movies to Facilitate Students' Reflection on Learning Experiences
abstract: We instructed students to use a 360-degree camera to record their own learning activity and to reflect on the activity. Students recorded their activity by themselves and reflected on it by watching it using a virtual reality (VR) goggle. Observing the students watching the activity by using a VR goggle and interviewing them showed that the students experienced high realistic sensation. The results implied that such a sense of immersion would encourage students to notice new aspects of their own experience and improve reflective ability.

articleTitle: A Virtual Reality Application for Primary School Mathematics Class
abstract: As one of the latest innovations in recent years, virtual reality (VR) opens new horizons for basic education areas. It provides learners opportunities to immerse themselves in visualized learning scenes and to interact with learning materials that distance, time, or safety factors make unavailable. In order to further promote the integration of novel information technology and primary mathematics education. A practical VR course was proposed with a focus on the magic Mobius strip for primary students. A detailed teaching procedure was also provided to describe how to appropriately use VR technology to support the learning experience. This study could provide teachers and educational researchers with teaching instruction ways of integrating VR technology into primary mathematics class.

Author Keywords: virtual reality, mathematics education, VR education, primary class

articleTitle: The Influence of Grouping/Non-grouping Strategies Upon Student Interaction in Online Forum: A Social Network Analysis
abstract: Interaction is the core of online learning activities, and online discussion forum is an important tool for students' interaction. In online forums, there are usually two organizing strategies for interaction: grouping and non-grouping. This study adopted experimental research and social network analysis method to analyze the interaction in two online forums respectively organized under grouping and non-grouping strategies. In the grouped forum, it was found that students' interaction was limited, but they were more closely connected in a same group, and received more equal attention. On the other hand, the enthusiasm of students to participate in the forum showed a downward trend as the course progressed; In addition, they replied to themselves more. While in the non-grouped forum, students tended to communicate with different students in early and late stage of the course, and they formed some close associations spontaneously in the process of communication. There were obvious "star" students and "neglected" students. Besides, students' enthusiasm to participate in the forum showed an upward trend as the course went on.

articleTitle: Implementation of ICT in Education in Indonesia During 2004-2017
abstract: Implementation of ICT in Education is an urgent thing and an accurate strategy in this era. Nevertheless, nowadays Indonesia still is one of the countries that has less development of ICT in education. Indonesia is a country of a thousand islands which are separated by an ocean which is the main obstacle to ICT infrastructure development in areas outside the main island (Java Island). Gaps in human resources and lack of teacher competency have also become an essential matter when implementing ICT in Education. On the other hand, Hong Kong and Singapore, as developed countries, already have useful infrastructure technology, and the human resources are qualified, so the implementation of ICT in Education is much more advanced compared to Indonesia. This paper focuses on identifying the application of ICT in Education, especially in Indonesia between 2004 and 2017 and analyzes the problems that occur. It suggests appropriate measures that can support successful ICT implementation in Education in Indonesia based on relevant studies.

Index Terms: Information And Communication Technology In Education

articleTitle: Eye-Tracking Data Analyzer (EDA) Developed for Educational Researchers: A Sample Module of LSA
abstract: Eye-tracking technology has been increasingly utilized as a research tool in educational studies in the last decade. However, analyzing eye-tracking data is usually a challenge for educational researchers. This study developed a tool, Eye-tracking Data Analyzer (EDA), for educational researchers to conduct advanced eye-tracking data analyses. With a graphical user interface, the EDA was developed by MATLAB programming. As a sample module of EDA, the development, interface design and validation of a lag sequential analysis (LSA) model were introduced. The LSA module in EDA provides a useful and convenient tool for educational researchers to quickly and deeply explore and illustrate learners' visual-attention transitional patterns during learning process. Implications and applications of the module are also briefly discussed in this study.

articleTitle: Development of a Digital Citizenship Computer Game with a Contextual Decision-Making-Oriented Approach
abstract: Worldwide counties foster good digital citizenship practices as a priority for students to be safe and responsible with technology use at an earlier age. With the advancement of computer and communication technologies, a computer game has been recognized to enable students' learning performance. However, situating students in meaningful computer game-based learning activities remains to be settled, especially for digital citizenship. In this study, a computer game with a contextual decision-making-oriented approach has been developed to support digital citizenship practices. An experiment was conducted on secondary school students to evaluate the effects of the proposed game on digital citizenship practices and learning motivation by comparing with the conventional learning approach. Interestingly, the experimental results indicated that the proposed game effectively reduced students' anxiety and promoted self-efficacy. Furthermore, it is also found that the proposed game benefited the males more than females in the term of learning motivations. This suggests the need to provide additional support to females' motivation in the further improvement of the proposed game.

articleTitle: A Study on the Appearances and Functionalities of Education Robots for Attracting Students' Attention and Interactive Interests
abstract: This research aims to study the appearance factors and functionalities of an education robot which may attract students' attention and their willingness to interact with the robot. With the rapid development of science and technology, the application of multimedia technology in education is becoming popular and vita. Thus, researchers believe education robots will improve learning experiences and enhance the learning efficiency of children. Besides, studies found that good-look anthropomorphic robots would enhance the acceptance of students as well. This research studies four different groups of students, i.e. junior-grade, middle-grade, senior-grade, and undergraduate, on their responses and interactions with an education robot. The research results show that junior-grade students prefer a toy-like robot with cute-design; middle-grade students care about the appearance of anthropomorphic robots; senior-grade students will keep interest in a robot if its responses are non-repeating; and undergraduate students will care about the functionalities of an education robot. Moreover, research also found that there is a relationship between the age of students and interactive behaviours as well.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Flipped Classroom Model Based on MOOC in the Course PHP Dynamic Website Development
abstract: For solving problems encountered in the PHP course, MOOC Embedded Flipped Classroom Model is proposed in this paper, which will make up for the shortage of the existing course. The basic model is analyzed and designed, specially the organization of the classroom activities in the process of the implementation of the model. Teaching design is carried out from the stage of resource construction, pre-class preparation, independent study, classroom communication, evaluation and feedback. By comparative analysis of students' achievement in 2014 and 2015, and the questionnaire survey for students' satisfaction with the flipped classroom, the following conclusions are made: Advantage of Flipped Class room model based on MOOC is obvious, students' achievements, learning interest and learning ability are obviously improved, and this model is an effective teaching method.

Author Keywords: flipped classroom, MOOC, teaching model, PHP dynamic website development

articleTitle: Real-Time and Non-digital Feedback E-Learning Tool
abstract: This paper provides a new method for enhancing feedback to a lecturer while he/she is teaching in real-time. It is well accepted that interactive teaching enhances learning and critical thinking. However, in a practical situation the lecturer cannot continually ask if the students have any questions and students are normally hesitant to ask questions, especially with a large cohort. Various eLearning tools that provide feedback are available such the Poll Everywhere, Sli.do, Glisser, Turning Technologies ARS, OMBEA, Socrative, iClicker, ARS Nova, Top Hat, Shakespeak, Sendsteps and Via Response. They are well received by students, but these tools are digital in the sense that they are limited to multiple choice. With this new method, the student can highlight on their devices the part(s) that he/she does not understand, and the system provides a real-time analysis and feedback in the form of display on the lecturer's screen. This device has been built and tested on a small number of students and the feedback from staff and students is very encouraging.

articleTitle: A Research on the Effect of Smartphone Use, Student Engagement and Self-Directed Learning on Individual Impact: China Empirical Study
abstract: The smartphone makes opportunities to extend teaching and learning locations from traditional classrooms to almost anywhere. This study examines the interrelation among smartphone use, student engagement, self-directed learning and individual impact of phone users. This study proposes a theoretical model integrating the technology acceptance model and D&M IS Success Model. The model is empirically validated through a quantitative method of structural equation modeling (SEM). The results show that (1) smartphone use and self-directed learning have significant positive effects on individual impact, (2) smartphone use and student engagement have significant positive effects on SDL, and (3) smartphone use has a significant positive effect on student engagement.

articleTitle: Connected Classroom Climate in Higher Education: A Scoping Review
abstract: The introduction of Dwyer et al.'s [1] Connected Classroom Climate Inventory (CCCI) began a seminal divergence of research focusing toward student-to-student socialization and behavior in educational environments. Connected classroom climate research has provided meaningful direction for improving instructional processes in face-to-face environments for nearly fifteen years. However, understanding of student-to-student connectedness is lacking in modern technology-mediated environments–arguably where student-to-student connectedness is most needed. This study presents a synthesis of peer-reviewed journal articles [2-17] that empirically utilized the CCCI within face-to-face, hybrid, and online environments to support future research on this important topic.

articleTitle: Addressing the Challenges in Engineering Classes: Harnessing Active Learning in a Robotics Course
abstract: Teaching Engineering, particularly fundamental courses and concepts, in higher education is always a challenge. Uninteresting lectures, static slides, abstract and mathematical concepts make engineering classes unattractive. This study presents a new active "hands-on lecture" lecturing approach to teaching robotics. The design-based research on the curriculum design has been conducted, and the active hands-on learning activities have been introduced. The development and class implementation of a real robot arm with course tailor-made tablet application is shown. The engagement of students in the learning process has been investigated.

articleTitle: Blended Learning with Multimedia e-Learning in Organic Chemistry Course
abstract: In traditional chemistry courses, they normally include lectures, tutorials and laboratory sections. In an undergraduate course "Advances in Organic Chemistry", it covers a wide range of advanced information in organic chemistry, including reaction mechanisms, strategies for synthetic methods and their applications to the synthesis of natural products. The purpose of this course is to help students develop advanced knowledge of synthetic tools, and to learn how to apply these theoretical strategies to real examples. We tried to develop a blended learning mode with e-components in this course, attempting to combine the best features of the traditional distance learning and face-to-face modes of teaching with the incorporation of multimedia videos (demonstration of laboratory techniques and experiments) and interactive web-based components (online lab quiz, interactive discussion board and electronic copy of study units). In this course, we would like to enhance and develop students' ability to understand and perform chemistry experiments. These materials are better to be prepared in multimedia video with the demonstration of experiments that can be described more clearly compared with just using textbook and lecture notes. Students can perform laboratory experiments by themselves on laboratory classes after learning these techniques in the video.

articleTitle: Perceptions and Utilization of a Learning Management System: An Analysis from Two Perspectives
abstract: This explorative study captured the subjective experiences and perceptions of faculty members and students regarding to the implementation of a new technology enhanced learning program in one university. Strategies used in the data collection included a custom-made set of online surveys, followed by informal interviews with faculty members and students. The findings showed some disparity exists between the experiences and perceptions of faculty and students with regards to some of the factors of the blended learning implementation. Since these experiences and perceptions define the attitudes of these two stakeholders in using the learning management system (LMS), addressing the disparity will be beneficial to encourage the productive use of this technology and crucial in the sustainable integration of LMS into the curriculum of this higher education institution (HEI).

Author Keywords: Blended Learning, Learning Management System, Analysis and Perceptions

articleTitle: Application of Flipped Classroom in College Computer Experiment Course
abstract: This paper introduces a teaching experiment research on the application of Flipped Classroom in a college computer experiment course. The participants are college students majoring in Educational Technology, and "Database Foundation" is an experiment course for them. The research group was made up of a teacher and five assistants. The teaching content was "Basic Operation on Microsoft Access Database". Some micro videos were made and uploaded to a network platform by the research group before experiment. Before class, students were asked to learn the content with videos and do some exercises. In class, the teacher answered the questions of students and guided students' operations on computers. Students can communicate with teachers and other students online whenever they want. After the experiment, an investigation was made on the effect.

Author Keywords: computer experiment course, flipped classroom, knowledge internalization

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on Recent Educational Policy Changes of Primary and Secondary Schooling in Hong Kong and Macau
abstract: Hong Kong and Macau are two cities which share many common features. For example, both are located in south coast in China, colonies of European countries for more than a century, Special Administrative Regions (SARs) in China, small in area, etc. The main differences are obvious: Hong Kong is considerably larger in terms of population and land area, a key role in financial field, whereas Macau is a gambling-based economic and known as the "Las Vegas" in the East. It has been about two decades since the reunification of both Hong Kong and Macau to China. The political, social and economic environments have been significantly changed. One main change is that China now becomes the world's second-largest economy and more influential in the policy making of two SARs. This paper attempts to explain the differences and similarities of educational policy changes of primary and secondary schooling in Hong Kong and Macau in recent years. Since the educational policies play an essential role in many social issues such as shaping national identity, social justice, etc, it is important to investigate how are they changed in recent year and understand the implications of such changes.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Virtual Simulation Teaching System of Solar System
abstract: The virtual simulation technology has been widely used in medical surgery, tourism teaching, military training and education. We summarize the characteristics and principles of developing a virtual simulation teaching system (VSTS). And we develop a system named as the virtual teaching simulation system of solar system model, which is based on Windows development platform, Visual C++6.0 used as the development environment, and OpenGL used as the graphics device interface. The system aims to cultivate students' spatial imagination, creative thinking ability and stimulate students to explore the mysteries of the universe.

articleTitle: Exploration and Practice Blended Ratio of Probability Theory and Mathematical Statistics Course
abstract: This paper takes Probability Theory and Mathematical Statistics course as an example, and takes WeChat public platform as the carrier, discusses the blended ratio of time between online learning and face-to-face teaching, and makes a study on teaching effect by using group comparison method. The results show that blended ratio 2: 6 is significantly better than 1: 6, 3: 6 and 0: 6 for online learning and face-to-face teaching. The results have some significance for improving the utilization rate of existing educational resources, allocating teaching time rationally and improving teaching quality.

Author Keywords: blended learning, blended ratio, face-to-face teaching, online Learning

articleTitle: An Empirical Study on the Users' Continuance Intention About MOOC: Based on Attachment Theory
abstract: As one of the main forms of online education, MOOC (Massive Open Online Course) has become more and more prominent in the field of online education due to its diversification of resources, perceived ease of use about courses, wide popularity in society and so on. However, there are some problems at the same time such as high dropout rate. In this research, we construct the research model on learners' continuance intention combining the theory of attachment and the theory of social technology system. The continuance intention is positively influenced by word of mouth, personalization service, telepresece, functional attachment, emotional attachment. Finally, according to the result of empirical analysis, the study makes suggestions for MOOC platforms. The implications of the findings are discussed

Author Keywords: Continuance Intention, Attachment Theory, Word of Mouth

articleTitle: College Students' Learning Outcomes in Flipped Classroom Instruction: A Literature Review
abstract: This study describes an overview of the effects of flipped classroom instruction on students' learning outcomes and provides direction for future research on this topic. The Web of Science was used to search for research and 22 relevant articles were identified [1-22]. The content analysis method was employed to examine the selected articles. The results showed that flipped classroom instruction can positively influence students' cognitive, affective, and self-regulated learning. Flipping the classroom can not only practice students' problem-solving and independent study abilities, but also provide students with a positive attitude toward learning.

articleTitle: Computer-Assisted Teaching Environment for Digital Signal Recognition Course Learning
abstract: In this paper, we present a computer-assisted teaching system for digital signal recognition using the computer as an interactive partner in problem solving activities. The software is designed to help students solve problems according to their own decision, or those arranged by their instructor. It can be used as a tool for digital signal course learning, spectrum recognition training, optical data processing, and providing feedbacks and advice upon request. The system includes an interactive interface, a spectrum simulator for graphical display of students' spectrum, a database which contains data of chemical groups and related information. The results showed that the developed system was effective in improving students' ability in spectrum interpretation.

articleTitle: The Supporting Environment Evaluation Model of ICT in Chinese University Teaching
abstract: With the rapid development of ICT and the increasing emphasis on ICT in education in many countries, ICT in teaching has become more and more significant. The related studies of supporting environment of ICT in university teaching mainly focused on the current situation and improvement strategies. They seldom studied the composition of supporting environment of ICT in university teaching from a systematic perspective. And a unified system model of supporting environment was scarce. The study divided the supporting environment of ICT in teaching into three categories of hardware environment, software environment and potential environment by analyzing the environmental factors of ICT in Chinese university teaching, and built the evaluation model of supporting environment of ICT in university teaching. Based on the model, the study evaluated the construction of supporting environment of ICT in teaching of the selected university in China to help make decisions for development of ICT in university teaching. This study could provide some reference for the related research and development of supporting environment of ICT in Chinese university teaching.

Index Terms: Information And Communication Technology In Education

articleTitle: New University Students and Blended Learning Experience
abstract: Blended Learning demands have been discussed and examined by academicians at the Faculty of Informatics and Management, University of Hradec Kralove for more than two decades. If blended learning is applied appropriately, it con-tributes to the increase in the efficiency of the educational process, to the decrease in the amount of face-to-face instruction and to the strengthening the dimension of self-study and project activities. The point is whether students coming from secondary schools are ready to use the offered eLearning tools and the potential to the full. The objective of the paper is to present trends in areas that are crucial for further blended learning use for university study purposes.

articleTitle: Robots – Stimulating Interest and Motivating Learning in Science and Technology
abstract: Nowadays the importance of science and technology is recognized all around the world. Especially for the students, how to arouse their interest and inspire their motivation toward science and technology becomes a hot topic for researchers and educators. The aim of the study is to evaluate how a robot (or a group of robots) can stimulate college students' interest in science & technology and motivate them to learn science & technology. A case study was conducted in the Macau University of Science and Technology where robots were brought in the campus in September 2017. An online questionnaire survey was carried and the data were analyzed by using SmartPLS. Results show that the appearance and functionality of robots have positive effects on the interest in robots, and the interest in robots further influences the interest in science and technology, then, it finally motivates students to learn science and technology.

Author Keywords: robot, science and technology, interest, motivation

articleTitle: How Students Prepare in Flipped Classrooms: A Case Study in a Physiology Class
abstract: The purpose of this study is to give suggestions on how faculty should design flipped classrooms. We conducted questionnaire and student interviews to clarify how students prepared for a physiology class at Kyoto University. The results of the questionnaire suggest that while there was a positive correlation between the preparation times and grades, some students' preparation was unproductive or inefficient. Therefore, we conducted interviews with five students to clarify the obstacles for achieving an efficient preparation. Interviews showed that one student didn't prepare at all, while the other four spent too much time on preparation without all of them achieving a high score. Not everyone recognized the significance of preparation. Additionally, four students deployed two note-taking styles - they either copied almost every word from the slides or summarized the important points from the slides. On the other hand, a student with no preparation was able to achieve average grades merely by reviewing the learning contents after the class. We found that students didn't know how to prepare appropriately for a flipped classroom, therefore it is important for instructors to specify clearly what areas students should focus on and how to efficiently take notes during their preparation.

articleTitle: Development and Evaluation of Interface for Screen Operation for Smooth Practical Training Using ICT in Elementary and Secondary Education
abstract: In practical training, which utilizes Information Communication Technology (ICT) in elementary and secondary education, teachers have difficulty in moving to students' seats while having to concentrate on the operation of educational display systems. Consequently, teachers tend to have fewer face-to-face interactions with students during training, making it difficult for them to perceive students' levels of understanding. Moreover, it is difficult to operate a computer screen using both hands to explain the practical training because the conventional interface device is operated using one hand. To solve these problems, we proposed and implemented an interface for screen operation. In addition, we conducted actual practical training utilizing ICT by using the interface for screen operation and evaluated the effectiveness of the proposed interface. From the results of this evaluation, we showed the effectiveness of the proposed interface for screen operation.

articleTitle: BlueJ-UML: Learning Object-Oriented Programming Paradigm Using Interactive Programming Environment
abstract: Most of the students coming from various different backgrounds find software programming a difficult subject to learn and master, especially in learning the concept of object-oriented programming. Because they must be able to model physical beings into virtualized objects and define complex object relationships in their designs for object interactions in a very abstract fashion that is not easily understood. This study is an attempt to introduce a unique interactive learning platform to students learning Java programming, which was designed with a set of object-oriented programming pedagogical considerations in mind. This study further extends and enhances with model-driven software development technique, such that to supporting unified modelling language (UML) class diagrams and code fragments generation in order to ease the learning needs of students, a unique way to learn fundamental programming concepts. This paper introduces a new online interactive platform and environment called BlueJ-UML, which is to help students to learn and practice object-oriented programming in class. It also evaluates the success outcome of the proposed new learning method through a Technology Acceptance Model Framework, and that followed by a comprehensive statistical analysis to assess improved academic performance of the students. The result was encouraging: student programming capability had been significantly elevated and was positively correlated to their overall perception and adoption of this new technique introduced in the class.

Author Keywords: Interactive Programming Environment, Object-oriented Programming, Technology Acceptance Model, Online Platform and Environment

articleTitle: The Classification of Teachers' Knowledge of 1-to-1 Elementary Education
abstract: In this study, we interviewed elementary school teachers about the use of Information Communications Technology (ICT) in the classroom. In this elementary school, a 1-to-1 tablet PC program was in place. Interview contents were analyzed using the TPACK framework. Among the classified forms of knowledge, Technical Knowledge (TK), Technical Pedagogical Knowledge (TPK), Technical Content Knowledge (TCK), and Technical Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) were further classified as "conventional teaching tools" or "1-to-1" depending on the object of knowledge. As per the result, among the seven knowledge types, the proportion is biased toward TPK, TCK, and TK; in particular, the proportion of TPK is high. In addition, a knowledge of the "1-to-1" was considered TPK, TCK, and TK.

Author Keywords: 1-to-1 tablet PCs, Teaching Knowledge, Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge

articleTitle: Promoting Self-Regulated Learning by Online Educational Resources
abstract: This paper investigates the students' self-regulated learning in primary education when traditional teaching method, which is teacher-centered in a classroom, is replaced with online educational resources. Various online educational resources such as videos, simulations and learning games are readily available on the Web. In addition, mobile and classroom technologies, such as portable devices can be considered as teaching tools in education. The good use of these educational resources and technologies cannot only assist students' formal classroom learning, but also cultivate the self-regulated learning of students. The i-Classroom implemented in a primary school adopted a new teaching method, which made use of the online educational resources and information technology, to achieve this goal. A survey (Sample size N = 149) was conducted to investigate the effectiveness of promoting self-regulated learning in three key aspects: learning motivation, planning and management, and self-monitoring. The result shows the current situation of the self-regulated learning of primary school students and discusses how i-Classroom can help students to enhance their ability to conduct self-regulated learning.

Author Keywords: self-regulated learning, educational resources, learning motivation, planning and management, self-monitoring

articleTitle: The Collaboration of Flipped Classroom and Jigsaw Model to Improve the Student's Character in Elementary School in Jakarta
abstract: Learning model helps learners to get information, ideas, skills, way of thinking and develop the attitude or character. The teacher's challenge is to select and use learning models that are appropriate to the needs of the 21st-century students. This study offers the application of collaborative learning models from Flipped Classroom and Jigsaw which are expected to develop the character of students at the elementary level in Jakarta. The model is the answer to the problems of students living in a rapidly evolving technology era and requires an active, creative, and collaborative learning model. The research design and data collection techniques used the Pre-experimental Design model with One Group Pretest-Posttest Study by observing and measuring the students' attitude over a period of time using character observation sheets, then the results were analyzed using descriptive percentage analysis to confirm or reject the initial hypothesis, answering research questions, and drawing conclusions. The research finds that teachers play an important role in developing the character of students through the design and model of learning used, the growth of the character of the treated class students are higher than the untreated class so that the value of the characters in the treated class in the category of very good and entrenched, the N-gain score average of the treated class is higher than that of the untreated class but the difference is not significant. Students also report on the positive impact of technology utilization and improvement of skills gained on learning using flipped classroom and jigsaw models.

articleTitle: Postgraduate's Personal Knowledge Management Using Cloud Services
abstract: Due to an emphasis on postgraduate's expectation regarding academic quality, various learning strategies have been proposed. In this study, the process of personal knowledge management and cloud services are used to encourage personalized learning on the selected knowledge topics. Adapted from prior learning process and PKM models, the proposed PKM model is developed comprising a series of stages: learning engagement, creating concept, building personal knowledge base and applying knowledge. Of the two groups, a total of 19 postgraduate students taking a "Applications of ICT" course of Knowledge Management program at Chiang Mai University, Thailand were the sample of a study, each of which was conducted over a 2-month period. The results revealed that there was no significant difference in a mean score between two groups on the test of understandings on the given knowledge topics, showing the students' average test score to exceed the minimum pass mark. The students' satisfaction level on personalized learning as supported by the PKM was also high.

articleTitle: Development of Smartphone Application "Family Portfolio" for Parent Development
abstract: We developed a family portfolio system (FP) that aims at promoting "parental awareness (PA)" and "interpersonal interaction themes (IIT)." In FP, users can store pictures with a type tag and an emotion tag. One month's use of FP suggested that parenting of "Awareness of a child" and "Non-parent role" were improved. The functions of "Recording", "Viewing", "Family newspaper" leads to the feeling that "I was able to look back on the growth of children." And "Viewing," "Family newspaper" leads to the feeling that "What newly noticed about child's growth," "I was able to look back on childcare".

Author Keywords: informal learning, e-portfolio, parenting, parent development

articleTitle: Comparison of Required Times and Awareness in Classes Through Creation of Storytelling and Product Introduction Slides
abstract: In order to ensure that university students have a sound base of computer knowledge and operating ability, and in order to improve their consciousness regarding their abilities, two types of classes were offered in which storytelling and product slide presentations were performed by creating slides using PowerPoint, entering consciousness and evaluations by others using Excel, and creating and submitting reports using Word. This paper investigates differences in the outcomes resulting from differences in the themes, and explores potential reasons for these differences. It compares and examines the amount of time taken to complete the works and the awareness of the students with regard to these abilities.

Author Keywords: storytelling, product presentation, slide creation, awareness regarding abilities, higher education

articleTitle: Effects of Familiar Faces in Video Modelling on Learning Effectiveness
abstract: In the past decade, it has become popular to use instructional videos for teaching and learning in online and blended learning environments. While researchers have studied how the presence of an instructor in an instructional video affects learning effectiveness, the influence of an instructor's visual familiarity toward students' learning is unclear. This experimental study explored how face familiarity in instructional videos affects the learning effectiveness of college students (n=47). Two sets of instructional videos were produced that adopted video modelling to teach business etiquette. The forty-seven college students each viewed one of the two video sets with cast that are respectively familiar faces and unfamiliar faces to the students. The results showed that participants can learn effectively from both sets of videos. Further examination showed face familiarity significantly reduced learning effectiveness, only when the participants had full-time work experience; otherwise, face familiarity does not have effect on learning effectiveness. These findings were explained in accordance to the Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning and indicate that face familiarity may hinder learning effectiveness.

articleTitle: Question-Based Idea Generation System for Writing Novels
abstract: Writing novels is one of the good trainings for cultivating the 21st century skills. However, some authors, especially beginners, cannot complete writing their novels. This research proposed a supporting method for completing the novels, especially in the phase of deriving the global scenario and the setting from the theme. We have analyzed the types of ideas that are needed to derive the global scenario and the setting, and the questions to focus on such ideas. In addition, based on the analysis, we have developed the support system in which authors can derive the ideas based on the given questions. The system also recommends the sequence of ideas from the derived ones that may form the scenario.

articleTitle: Diagnosing Individual University Students' Information Literacy Problems with a Concept-Effect Propagation-Oriented System
abstract: With the rapid growth of technologies and internet broadband, accessing digital information has been becoming more economical and convenient. Therefore, knowing and having the information literacy skills are crucial, especially for students in the twenty-first century. Moreover, diagnostic systems, which have been used to analyze students' learning problems, are recognized as a significant tool to assist individual students in receiving their own guidance and improving the acquired skills. Consequently, this study developed a diagnostic system for diagnosing students' information literacy problems by applying a concept-effect propagation approach. Thirty-two undergraduate students were recruited to evaluate their perceptions toward the developed system. It was found that the students had positive perceptions and intended to use the developed system for improving their information literacy skills.

articleTitle: Designing a Teaching Model for the Flipped Classroom Based on Pads
abstract: Recently, the spring of new devices, the emergence of flipped classroom and the invention of Padagogy Wheel inspire us to explore the flipped model based on Pads. According to this teaching trend, in this article, we extract the teaching process of flipped classroom, with using Padagogy Wheel Theory as the method to design activities, Activity Theory as framework to analyze activities, Knowledge Integration Theory as a bridge to achieve integrated design, Bloom's Taxonomy of Educational Objectives to arrange the objectives of "online and offline" learning. Finally it is achieved by establishing a flipped model based on pads to help teachers flip their class successfully, and in further research, we will enrich this model to fit in different subjects and meet more teachers' demand based on practice.

articleTitle: Comparative Study on Networking Simulation Tools Using Correlation Analysis
abstract: Several researches were conducted and has proven the effectiveness and differences of network simulation tools such as Packet Tracer and Graphical Network Simulator. Simulation tools provide a means for the students to experience network configuration in a virtual environment and enhances their troubleshooting skills in the network architecture. This paper aims to provide a comparison in the transfer of knowledge from the simulated environment and the actual laboratory of Packet Tracer and Graphical Network Simulator 3(GNS3). An experimental approach was implemented to identify the performance of 30 students grouped into two. Each group was assigned a simulation tool but were given the same topology and network requirements. The instrument used to measure the configuration and troubleshooting skills were lifted from the Cisco Certified Network Entry Technician certification. Correlation analysis was applied in processing the data from students' scores. Results showed evidence on the transfer of skills from two environments and identified GNS3 as getting a higher percentage of knowledge transfer.

articleTitle: Support System for Discovering Laws of Motion in Learning Physics
abstract: The growing disinterest in science among young people has become a serious problem. Students do not relate the theories and formulas learned in physics with real-world phenomena. The objective of this research is to propose introduction learning methods for students to discover laws of motion from the phenomena around them. In this learning method, real-world objects and motions are analyzed and common characteristics for these motions are extracted to form a law. Any contradiction in the created law is then investigated with other phenomena. We developed a system to achieve this learning method. In the system, learners use cameras to take photographs of physical phenomena, which encourages awareness of the physical phenomena around them. As the outcome of the analysis, the learners attach annotations to the photos that represent the motions and properties of the moving objects and surrounding objects. They then create a group of photos based on the same motion and develop a hypothesis of the law by selecting common annotations from the group. If the created hypothesis has a contradiction, the system sends a message to encourage the learners to rethink their hypothesis.

articleTitle: What are the Differences Among Pre-Service Teachers of Diverse Achievement Levels in Their Online Instructional Design Collaboration? — Analyzing from the Perspective of Behavior Pattern
abstract: Instructional design plays a vital role in the development of pre-service teachers. Sharing and communication based on instructional design is the norm of professional development of pre-service teachers. Based on the instructional design activities of pre-service teachers guided by the collaborative knowledge building, this research adopts the methods of lag sequence analysis and content analysis method to analyze and compare the participation and behavior pattern of 20 pre-service teachers in both high- and low-achievement groups. This is in order to analyze the differences of online behavior pattern among pre-service teachers of diverse achievement levels. Moreover, a few suggestions are put forward: We should encourage pre-service teachers in the low-achievement group to be more active in participating in various stages of collaborative knowledge building activities, and improve the ability of pre-service teachers in the low-achievement group to deeply reflect on themselves after consulting with members of their cohort.

Author Keywords: Collaborative Knowledge Building, Pre-Service Teachers, Online Behavior Patterns, Lag Sequence Analysis

articleTitle: Course Design for "Critical Thinking" in the Freshman Curriculum and Associated Assessment Strategies for Actively Engaged Learners
abstract: In this study, the course design and development for a freshman course to nurture students' critical thinking skills in the curriculum in social constructive paradigm, that is, a Problem-Based Learning model in teams were examined. Due to its nature, assessment strategies associated with team-based active learning model were also discussed. It is proposed, in the course of discussion, that the traditional evaluation conducted by instructors may not be suitable for the assessment of active learning. Rather, assessment strategies with rubrics have been proved to be optimal for such educational paradigms, which directly involve the main stakeholders of learning, namely, the learners.

Author Keywords: course design, course development, critical thinking, active learning, assessment strategies, rubrics, social constructivism

articleTitle: An Empirical Study on Factors Affecting Primary School Teachers' Use of LCS
abstract: The trend of using Learning Cyber Space is now rapidly expanding in China, which is expected to change the teaching and learning mode in primary and secondary school. Teachers' usage plays a key role in promoting the LCS. However, the teachers' registering rate of LCS is relatively high while the actual usage rate is low. The purpose of this study is to verified factors including learning resource, user-interface and function, perceived ease of use that affected primary school teachers' use of LCS. The result shown that user-interface and function and perceived ease of use have significant influence on the primary school teachers' use of LCS. Perceived ease of use was found as the most significant factor for usage of primary school teachers' LCS. Learning resource, however, has little impact on the primary school teachers' use of LCS. Implications of this finding are also discussed, which could provide some suggestions for the future development of LCS.

articleTitle: The Effects of Using E-Portfolio Data at Kansai University Writing Center
abstract: This study examined the effects of using an e-portfolio system to identify concerns raised during sessions at Kansai University Writing Center. The ratio of sessions whereby tutors asked students about their problems and progress was significantly high during sessions when users dropped in or were first-time repeaters. The results indicate that one of the e-portfolio systems used by Kansai University, TEC book, gathers and shares information about students and the historical data of instructional results, thus promoting the meeting at the beginning of sessions. Since both tutors and students cooperate in these sessions, it is important for tutors to quickly and easily understand students' concerns. E-portfolio systems such as TEC book can be one of the best kinds of support for writing sessions.

articleTitle: Teaching Practice of Combining MOOCs and Flipped Classroomon on a College Course
abstract: Nowadays, various techniques have been combined increasingly and applied into blended learning to improve students' learning outcomes. Based on a teaching practice of Modern Education Technology course in a normal college, this study was to analyze the complementary relationship between MOOCs and flipped classroom in teaching, and explore students' perception of this new teaching method so as to point out the challenges that this type of teaching method would face. A total of 158 students participated in this study, and both quantitative and qualitative research methods were adopted. Results from this study, on the one hand, students hoped to benefit from the teaching environment integrated with technology; on the other hand, the students' original learning habits and perspectives formed in their previous learning experience prevent them from quickly adapting to the new teaching method. What's more, the results showed that the main challenge of this teaching method was that the classroom environment couldn't provide immediate feedback to students. Concludes with recommendations that educators should teach students to solve the above-mentioned problems so as to contribute to more prominent advantages of new technologies.

articleTitle: Development and Assessment of E-Learning for Academic Writing: Learning Support of Writing Centers
abstract: This paper is a report on the design of Japanese writing in e-learning, based on the IDEAL model in undergraduate education. Construction of the IDEAL model involves the following steps: Identify problems and opportunities, define goals, explore possible strategies, anticipate outcomes and act, and look back and learn. We identified writing problems by 1) analyzing students' usage history of the writing center and 2) comparing freshmen's report before and after usage of the writing center in the first year. We then defined the problems based on the analyses and explored alternative solutions. To apply the solutions, an e-learning program, comprising 29 lessons, was developed to nurture Japanese writing skills at the undergraduate level. The e-learning program consisted of five categories: 1) "Before writing," 2) "Gathering information," 3) "How to write: sentence structure," 4) "How to write: sentence expressions," 5) "Reflecting on your report." These learning materials were also integrated with tutoring at writing centers and support faculty staff to teach effective writing lessons. Based on these analyses, we developed e-learning materials. This paper follows the process of developing and accessing web-based learning material for Japanese writing. According to the results of the questionnaire, the effectiveness of e-learning was revealed.

Author Keywords: e-Learning, learning support, academic writing, writing center

articleTitle: Virtual Dulcimer Auxiliary Teaching System Based on Musical Instrument Digital Interface
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid progress of game development technology as well as human-computer interaction technology, game-based learning (GBL) has not only drew the attention of increasing number of researchers but this method has also been implemented into classrooms by teachers around the world. And the improvement for knowledge acquisition is being reported as the most frequently occurring outcome of GBL across a wide range of subjects like mathematics, physics, health etc. However, there are very limited cases where GBL being employed into music class especially for Chinese traditional musical instruments which are facing the danger of being lost since children today are far less likely to have a chance to play or listen to those beautiful instruments because schools usually focus more on the education of mainstream instruments like pianos and violins. Therefore, the present paper designs and develops an interactive virtual dulcimer auxiliary teaching system based on musical instrument digital interface, which in the future can be utilized as a tool in class to assist teaching or can be promoted as a self-teaching instrument.

articleTitle: Learning Profiles, Behaviors and Outcomes: Investigating International Students' Learning Experience in an English MOOC
abstract: Learning analytics provided new opportunities to investigate students' online learning experience in a more in-depth and comprehensive way. In this study, learning analytics were utilized to investigate international students' learning experience in an English MOOC in addition to survey data and test results. Using K-means cluster analysis and stepwise linear regression, this study classified international MOOC students into four major categories and identified three types of learning behaviors as significant predictors for MOOC learning performance. The research findings provide several interesting perspectives on international students' online learning behaviors, and can inform the design and evaluation of online instruction for global audiences.

articleTitle: Visualizing and Understanding the Hotspots and Trends of Mobile Learning
abstract: The aim of the study is to visualize the status quo of the research on mobile learning via co-citation analysis. A total of 2392 papers were retrieved from the Web of Science database with full bibliographic records including authors, titles, abstracts, and reference lists. CiteSpace V was used to conduct visualization analysis about the research on mobile learning by identifying the most influential authors and essential papers, as well as research hotspots, and research frontiers in the field of mobile learning.

articleTitle: The Design and Practice of the Flipped Classroom Teaching Model Based on the Padagogy Wheel
abstract: With the development of the flipped classroom teaching practice, the demand of how to use iPad to teach effectively is increasingly important. It is not difficult to find out that from the Bloom's Digital Taxonomy and the micro perspective of learning activities, it is a theory introduction of how to effectively organize and use Apps to design classroom. Based on the activity theory, this study focuses on a typical digital tool oriented Bloom's taxonomy of educational objectives, the Padagogy Wheel, and the flipped classroom teaching model, and initially constructs a flipped classroom teaching model, including nine layers of structure: core literacy level, learning motivation level, teaching mode level, teaching goal level, behavioral verb level, activity level, activity analysis level, Apps tool level and SAMR level. On this basis, the case study method is adapted to verify the effectiveness of the model in education and teaching.

articleTitle: Online Case-Based Instruction: The Effects of Online Case Discussion and the Potential Influencing Factors
abstract: To explore the effects of online discussion on online case-based instruction (CBI), this study conducted a quasiexperiment to compare the learning performance measured by "problem space coverage" and learning experience of two groups of students (n=186) in a graduate level instructional design course. The empirical results show that the treatment group participating in online discussion activities showed significantly higher learning performance. Learning experience was similar between groups. In addition, investigation of the influencing factors in online CBI indicated that students' case viewing behaviors and the forum posting behaviors might lead to better learning performance.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Online and Printed Form of Testing in Scientific Reasoning and Metacognitive Monitoring
abstract: The article deals with exploitation of online and printed versions of tests in the field of scientific reasoning and metacognitive monitoring. The main objective is to prove whether results in both administration modes of testing are identical. However, designing online tests is less time and work demanding, and moreover, automatic evaluation tools can be used. Totally, 115 students were tested by Lawson's test. The received results were discussed with emphasis on designers of educational and curricular concepts of the pre-service teacher education, particularly reflecting students' low level of scientific reasoning and high value of absolute accuracy which indicates high level of inaccuracy in confidence judgement of their own performance compared to the real situation.

Author Keywords: Scientific Reasoning, Metacognitive monitoring, Online Test, Printed Test, Administration Mode
